newsitem.title: EGYPT: Eastern Company profits up in 95/96.
newsitem.headline: Eastern Company profits up in 95/96.

text.p: Egyptian cigarette manufacturing monopoly Eastern Company said on Sunday its after-tax profits rose to 145.820 million pounds ($42.9 million) in the financial year 1995/96, 2.9 percent up on 141.677 million in the previous year. The years end on June 30.
The firm earlier had earlier expected profits to fall to 120 million pounds ($35 million) in 1995/6.
After deducting reserves, profits for distribution are 123.056 million pounds, equivalent to 4.92 pounds for each of the 25 million shares, which last traded at 48.90 pounds.
The firm paid a dividend of 4.00 pounds for the financial year 1994/5. It has not yet announced a dividend for 1995/6.

The mostly state-owned company said production of all types of cigarettes exceeded the target by 15 percent to 45.622 billion cigarettes in 95/96. In the previous year, it produced 42.401 billion, also surpassing the target of 39.00 billion.
The firm has called a general assembly for December 7.
The value of net sales rose in 1995/6 rose to 1,433.50 million pounds from 1,316.79 million.
Last year the state privatised 2.5 million shares in Eastern Company, or 10 percent of the total equity, at prices ranging from 45 to 49 pounds.
